However compilation errors indicate they are not imported. Likely the test file missing import statements. Also annotations like @ExtendWith, @Mock, @BeforeEach, @Test need imports from JUnit5 and Mockito. Also missing java.util.* imports.

Also there are duplicate variable declarations in setupBeforeEach: they declare JsonNodePath path twice. Also they attempt to mock BaseJsonValidator but then override with TestValidator. The code is messy.

Simplify: we can just use TestValidator and not mock. Remove mocking code and duplicate variable declarations. Provide proper imports.

Also need import com.networknt.schema.* classes: BaseJsonValidator, JsonNodePath, SchemaLocation, JsonNode, JsonSchema, ValidatorTypeCode, ValidationContext, ValidationMessageHandler, ExecutionContext, ValidationMessage.

Also import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode? Actually JsonNode is from com.fasterxml.jackson.databind, but the library may have its own JsonNode alias. In networknt schema, they use com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode. So import that.

Also PathType is likely enum in JsonNodePath? Need import com.networknt.schema.PathType.

Also need import java.util.Collections, java.util.Set.

Now adjust code: In setupBeforeEach, just create a default validator instance: maybe using new TestValidator(null, new JsonNodePath(PathType.ROOT), null, null, null, null). No need for mock fields.

But the test uses mock fields for other tests? Not needed. Remove @Mock fields or keep but not used.

Simplify: Keep @Mock fields but we need to import them. However they refer to types not imported; we can keep them but they will compile if types exist. Provide imports.

Now fix duplicate variable declarations: rename second variable to pathRoot.

Better: In setupBeforeEach, just instantiate validator = new TestValidator(null, new JsonNodePath(PathType.ROOT), null, null, null, null);

Remove the mocking line.

Now adjust imports.

Now ensure code compiles.
